requirements.name: Selected-model transport
requirements.outcome: Eligible Pi publishes its current exact model ID and reference through the defined input protocol; unknown metadata clears instead of guessing. It never publishes a glyph or terminal-title suffix.
requirements.acceptance: checks the full wire method, source, allowed keys, values, reservation/readback, TTL, and null/invalid-input cases.

requirements.name: Preserved naming
requirements.outcome: Pi's title, session/project naming and other extensions' title behavior remain untouched through startup, delayed binding, rename and shutdown.
requirements.acceptance: supplies a title writer that throws on any call and verifies ordinary Unicode/naming state is unchanged.

requirements.name: Startup publication
requirements.outcome: Startup makes fresh selected-model metadata available independently of any default title write after binding, including delayed extension/resource binding.
requirements.acceptance: performs late host title writes around publication and verifies the same selected-model inputs/family without a title write from this extension.

requirements.name: Restored selection
requirements.outcome: Resume uses its fresh session-start context and reference; previous session data/callbacks cannot supply the restored model.
requirements.acceptance: changes model/reference, invalidates the old context, omits restore model events and verifies the restored family plus refusal of the old digest.

requirements.name: Model switch
requirements.outcome: Set/cycle replaces the former selected ID and glyph after accepted publication; same-model selection remains consistent. Latest pending selection wins over delayed earlier requests.
requirements.acceptance: checks recognized-to-recognized and rapid A→B→C transitions, delayed replies and same-model selection through the shipped consumer/output path.

requirements.name: Known family resolution
requirements.outcome: Only the matching occupant's selected ID determines Pi's family; the existing glyph keys and cells provide the mark.
requirements.acceptance: tests every table row and namespace leaf in font/text/none variants, including numeric Qwen IDs and the reasoning boundary.

requirements.name: Hermes/non-Pi compatibility
requirements.outcome: Non-Pi lookup, output and presentation remain semantically identical; no Hermes, palette/font or managed integration changes are made.
requirements.acceptance: compares old/new non-Pi regex/fallback fixtures and output snapshots exactly, and hashes protected artifacts.

requirements.name: Unknown/missing model clearing
requirements.outcome: Missing/invalid/unrecognized/expired or mismatched Pi input clears both model cells on the next successful frame and preserves the agent mark; it never caches the preceding family.
requirements.acceptance: covers known→unknown→known, TTL expiry, missing inputs, wrong reference and preserved Pi mark in fresh/stale rows.

requirements.name: No unrelated-text inference
requirements.outcome: Names, titles, provider labels, malformed identifiers, other agents and other sessions cannot supply a guessed Pi model.
requirements.acceptance: supplies family words/old suffix-like text in unrelated fields, near-prefix IDs, trailing slash, whitespace, controls, overlength IDs and foreign references; only a valid selected-ID input can resolve.

requirements.name: Lifecycle matrix
requirements.outcome: Startup/reload/new/resume/fork republish fresh state; rename does not change the model; shutdown retires old work. Session replacement cannot reuse an invalid context.
requirements.acceptance: covers those paths, name clearing, deferred old callbacks, both reference kinds and server token loss followed by fresh republishing.

requirements.name: Resource and extension compatibility
requirements.outcome: Factory/headless/outside-Herdr execution allocates nothing. An eligible session owns one refresh timer and serialized bounded socket work; shutdown releases them without changing the managed extension.
requirements.acceptance: checks zero factory/rpc/json/print resources, one unrefed timer, missing-environment refusal, repeated shutdown/reload, zero old sockets/timers, and duplicate-publisher/preflight refusal.

requirements.name: Privacy and payload safety
requirements.outcome: Only model ID, reference digest, sequence counter and source/host/glyph identities enter feature metadata/evidence. Counter files contain only the last reserved integer. No session file content/path, prompt, transcript, credential, user title or task name is persisted; no payload controls are normalized into another model.
requirements.acceptance: uses secret sentinels in forbidden inputs, checks exact allowed payload keys and generic diagnostics, and verifies control/Unicode/length rejection and digest construction.

requirements.name: Request-free pinned compatibility
requirements.outcome: Pi 1.0.4 and existing dependencies suffice; selection/readback does not require inference, authentication, discovery, upgrades, process spawning or bot changes.
requirements.acceptance: imports the shipped extension through the installed compatible loader and exercises it with forbidden provider/HTTP/process operations set to throw.

requirements.name: Failure, ordering and restart recovery
requirements.outcome: Socket refusal, partial/malformed/oversized replies, timeout, ignored sequences, clock changes and capacity refusals do not hang Pi, invent delivery or resurrect old state. Session loss fails closed; recoverable token loss republishes without a prompt.
requirements.acceptance: covers those failures, persistence-before-send, counter-write/rename/crash failures, corrupt/symlink/ownership refusal, reload after TTL expiry, server restart between requests followed by producer crash/reload, delayed old clears, sequence recovery without wall-clock assumptions, server reset, pane-not-found retirement, bounded cleanup and single generic warning.

requirements.name: Two-host deployment gate
requirements.outcome: Only an authorized deployer may activate the reviewed consumer first, then the byte-identical global native extension on each host after independent successful preflight. No unrelated files or integrations are altered.
requirements.acceptance: dry-runs both hosts; missing authority, native Pi, managed reference, model cell, glyph match, token/source capacity, input ownership, active consumer or idle activation safety must refuse mutation. It checks zero-counter provisioning before first activation with prior-publication evidence, refusing initialization without that evidence. Success verifies shipped source hashes and protected files.

requirements.name: Two-host visible acceptance
requirements.outcome: On each authorized existing idle native Pi pane, the selected known model's glyph is shown after Pi's mark; changing to an unknown selection removes only the model mark. No prompt/inference/new session/restart is needed.
requirements.acceptance: requires per-host automated selected-ID/reference/input/output/digest readbacks plus cropped sidebar evidence of adjacency and unknown clearing, in the actual configured visible glyph variant. Existing plain ink is valid. Offline tests are not this acceptance.

requirements.name: Safe rollback
requirements.outcome: Remove only the delivered global extension after authorization; activate removal through idle `/reload`, with no session/process restart or interruption. Retire publication, clear/expire ID/ref and preserve the invisible sequence counters, Pi's normal title, existing extensions and Hermes. Keep the fail-closed Pi consumer; never restore whole-title guessing.
requirements.acceptance: verifies file ownership, removal/reload discovery, unchanged session/PID/title, immediate successful clear versus failed-clear lease expiry, retained counters and safe reinstall without stale writes.

requirements.name: Bounded delivery
requirements.outcome: Deliver one feature through the ordered slices below, each with its own gate; hold live execution until authorized. Do not introduce a metadata service, integration replacement or additional-host rollout.
requirements.acceptance: dry-runs missing/failed earlier gates and verifies no consumer/extension activation or live action is reachable until its prerequisites and authority pass.
